item.title: Wajima Lacquerware: One of Japan's Most Prized Lacquer Traditions — Guide
item.description: Wajima-nuri, the lacquerware produced in and around Wajima on the Noto Peninsula, is considered one of Japan’s most prized lacquer traditions, renowned for its exceptional durability achieved through a painstaking application process that can involve well over 100 individual steps, including a distinctive undercoat reinforced with diatomaceous earth and cloth to strengthen the finished piece against daily wear. Visitors can try hands-on workshops in Wajima, working under artisan guidance to decorate or finish a small lacquerware piece, offering a hands-on introduction to a craft that traditionally takes years of apprenticeship to master.
